circle.statement: Pantheism is both directions at once: entity applied to Nature, and Nature rendered in entity. The model is of out-there; the modeling happens in-there. The work is reducing dissonance between the mapping and the mapped. Petition is a second map of the same mapped.
circle.lane_A: After the scientific revolution, first-rank physical work is almost never written as if a person outside the world may suspend the equations.
circle.lane_B: The circle, taught as geometric form in middle childhood into adolescence, can compound by cutting petition as a second map. Dividend is reduced dissonance, not a genius badge.

two_lane_paper.role: Primary paper. Lane A public description + Lane B labeled cultivation model.

paragraphs.text: Two Lanes: Position and Cultivation
A public description of where remembered genius sits, and a labeled model of the circle: mapping of out-there, rendered in-there, dissonance reduced
Neuresthetics Genius Study, Version 7.1
How to read this paper
This paper runs two lanes on the same instruments. They share a roster, a coherence rubric, and a construct called lawful immanent order. They do not share a standard of proof.
Table 0. The lanes are parallel, not sequential. Lane B is not the ‘real meaning’ of Lane A.

Lane B is the author’s religion stated as a model. Naming it that way is cleaner than smuggling it into the abstract as a finding. Readers who want only the public track can stop at the end of Lane A. Readers who want the compounding story must accept that it is labeled belief plus mechanism, not a result of the 482.
Shared instruments
Genius

Achievement, not a test score. Inclusion needs lasting original impact on documented criteria. Excluded: mastery without originality, transient fame, collectives, non-persons. Contemporaries may be provisional. The working roster is 482 unique names after alias resolution, built as a five-model aggregate (Claude, DeepSeek, Gemini, ChatGPT, Grok). Frequency is inter-model consensus after merge, not intensity of genius. Primary cuts: frequency ≥ 3 (core) and ≥ 2 (extended).
Coherence rubric

Seventy-seven schemas scored on five ten-point axes: consistency, paradox handling, empirical compatibility, evidence versus revelation, predictive success. Authorial map of official systems. Not an IQ test. Not a population parameter.
Lawful immanent order

Person-level region, not a church. High LIO: regular, non-intervening cosmos, no personal moral ledger, observation outranks revelation, no reserved exemptions. Spinoza is the prototype of the circle, not of a deletion: Deus sive Natura is entity applied to Nature and Nature rendered in entity. The model is of out-there; the modeling happens in-there; the work is reducing dissonance between the mapping and the mapped. Einstein used that prototype and declined the sectarian word. Atheistic naturalism is a neighbor on exemptions and a disagreement about the entity-term. Classical theism can sit mid-to-high on lawfulness without identity of God and world. Heritage stays off the outcome.
LANE A  —  PUBLIC TRACK
Lane A. Where remembered genius sits
A1. Two observations, not yet one cause

In living samples, strength of religious belief covaries modestly and negatively with measured intelligence. Typical magnitudes are r ≈ −0.20 to −0.24 for belief rather than attendance (Zuckerman, Silberman, and Hall; later updates; Stagnaro and colleagues). Analytic cognitive style is a leading mediator (Gervais and Norenzayan; Pennycook and colleagues). This is a small replicated covariance. It is not a sorting of historical genius.

In the historical record, as read qualitatively from the high-consensus physical-science core, paradigm-shifting work after the seventeenth century rarely takes a miracle-working personal God as the working metaphysics of the theory. Faraday and Maxwell are devout and lawful; they force the phrase working metaphysics rather than baptism. This sentence is a pattern awaiting LIO coding, not a completed count.
A2. Three hypotheses, left open
Cultivation. Occupying LIO early reduces dissonance and raises later output. Lane B develops this as a model. Lane A does not treat it as shown.
Selection. Integrative intelligence independently discards petitionary gods. Living-sample analytic-style results sit most naturally here.
Attractor. The world is approximately Spinoza-shaped: one order, modeled out-there, rendered in-there. Accurate maps converge. Intelligence is the capacity to notice.
A roster of the dead can describe position. It cannot separate H1, H2, and H3. It cannot turn a present-day headcount of identifiers into an incidence rate. No G / P_2025 ranking is part of Lane A.
A3. Analytic plan
Composition by era and field, among people who already cleared the genius bar. No population denominator.
Same-century elite baseline if a contrast is required, never a 2025 world-religion stock.
Childhood tradition versus adult working ontology, certainty-gated at ≥ 0.6.
Within-tradition distance from interventionism (Maxwell against popular Victorian Anglicanism; Ibn Sina against popular kalam).
First coding pool: frequency ≥ 3, physical science 1600–1950, mid-basin theists coded first as a stress test.

Four limited claims Lane A is willing to carry now: the living-sample r; the qualitative clustering of working metaphysics in later physical theory; the adjacency of atheistic naturalism and Spinozism on exemptions (not identity of the entity-term); the existence of first-rank mid-basin theists. Nothing else.
A4. What Lane A refuses
Pantheism at any geniuses-per-million figure.
A correlation between coherence scores and historical fertility treated as a population fact.
An IQ treatment effect from conversion.
Heritage as worldview (Einstein and Feynman are not JUDA by working ontology).
LANE B  —  BELIEF TRACK
Lane B. How early LIO could compound
Status of this lane. Conviction plus mechanism. Not licensed by Lane A. Written so that a later measurement can kill it.
B1. The claim, in one paragraph

A child mind defaults toward agents and purposes. Promiscuous teleology and hypersensitive agency detection make a personal, intervening God the easy early schema, not the hard one. Lawful immanent order is therefore an override, not a setting the child arrives at alone. Pantheism’s version of the override is not “there is no one to petition.” It is the circle: the thunder is in entity because it is, and the model of thunder is of something out-there. Petition is a category error because it splits the mapped from the mapping. If that override is installed while networks that hold self, world, and explanation are still plastic — and if it is practiced in geometric form, as definitions and consequences without reserved exemptions — the person spends the rest of life tightening one map instead of running two. The dividend is reduced dissonance between mapping and mapped, not a test point.

Pantheism in this lane is both: entity applied to Nature, and Nature in entity. That is why the word God stays, and why “all in your head” is only true if head means the one entity doing the rendering. The geometric method is the practice that makes a mismatch expensive. Neuresthetics is the later adult loop that keeps closing it: map, modulate, watch a proxy, repeat.
B2. Why childhood is the interesting version of cultivation

Adult conversion to LIO can still be selection: the work already taught the person that exemptions do not help. Childhood LIO, if it happens, is different. It would be a schema in place before the person has a field. That is the only version of H1 that could pay ‘for life’ rather than pay as a side-effect of already doing science.

The developmental literature, read in this spirit rather than as a citation dump, cuts against comfort. Young children explain nature with purpose and agency more readily than with mechanism. An early pantheist household is swimming upstream. That makes the belief track more demanding, not less. If LIO were the spontaneous metaphysics of childhood, early exposure would explain nothing. Because it is not, early exposure — if it works — would be doing real work against a default.
B3. The geometric method as the active ingredient

Content and form can come apart. A child can be told ‘God is nature’ or ‘nature is in God’ as a sentence and still keep a petitionary God in practice. The geometric method is the form that makes the circle expensive to betray: say what a thing is, say what follows, do not reserve a second map for weather, illness, or the in-group. That form is close to what later physical theory demands. Faraday already had most of the form without the metaphysics. Lane B’s distinctive claim is that having the form early, under a metaphysics that does not fight it, compounds; having the form only when the profession requires it is selection.

If later practice trials show that geometric reasoning without the metaphysics produces the same proxies as geometric reasoning with it, Lane B should drop the religion and keep the method. If the metaphysics adds nothing measurable, it remains a way of life and loses its claim on dividends.
B4. A compounding sketch, not a wiring diagram
Default. Early cognition prefers agents and purposes.

Override window. A household or teacher installs the circle — one map of out-there, rendered in-there, no reserved petitioner — while self/world models are still being laid down. The practice window named for this study is middle childhood into adolescence, when geometric form can actually be used.
One-model advantage. Later scientific or philosophical work does not require a second reconciliation step. Attention stays on the structure.
Practice maintenance. The adult loop — geometric reading, definition before inference, feedback from a proxy — keeps the override from rotting back into petition.

Visible dividend. Not ‘genius.’ Lower dissonance between mapping and mapped, faster rejection of a second map, less rumination about cosmic exception. Exceptional work remains rare and still needs talent, institution, and luck.

This sketch does not name a single network as the site. Default-mode language in the wider program is a pointer at self-world integration, not a measured target. Lane B should talk about named proxies — a rumination scale, a dissonance diary, an analytic-task battery, HRV if someone insists on a body measure — until a specific circuit earns its keep.
B5. Predictions that can fail
Table B1. Lane B lives or dies by these, not by Einstein’s frequency count.
B6. What would not count as support
A 2025 pantheist headcount under a handful of historical names.
The living-sample religiosity–IQ correlation, which is mostly selection-shaped and adult.
The author finding the story beautiful. Beauty is allowed in Lane B as motive. It is not evidence.
Coding the physical-science core as high-LIO after the fact and calling that a childhood effect.
B7. Relation to the practice program

Neuresthetics as loop — identification, intentional modulation, feedback — is the adult maintenance step in B4. It can be run by someone who never accepted the metaphysics. Lane B’s religion is the claim that starting the loop inside LIO, early, is better than starting it as a repair. That claim needs families, schools, or a long prospective cohort. It does not need another ranking of the dead.
Joint close

Lane A says: here is a map and a method for reading remembered minds without a fertility table. Lane B says: pantheism is the circle of mapping and mapped — out-there modeled in-there — and teaching that as geometric form in the developmental window can compound by cutting petition as a second map; here is how to find out that this is wrong.

The author holds Lane B. The paper does not launder that holding through Lane A. If the two lanes ever converge, they will converge on a measurement that was named in advance: timing on the roster, or a practice trial with a proxy, or a developmental contrast that survives education as a control. Until then they stay in their lanes.
References
Barrett, Justin L. Why Would Anyone Believe in God? Walnut Creek: AltaMira, 2004. Agency-detection account of the child default.
Gervais, Will M., and Ara Norenzayan. “Analytic Thinking Promotes Religious Disbelief.” Science 336, no. 6080 (2012): 493–496.
Kelemen, Deborah. “Are Children ‘Intuitive Theists’?” Psychological Review 111, no. 2 (2004): 295–301. Promiscuous teleology.
Pennycook, Gordon, et al. “Analytic Cognitive Style Predicts Religious and Paranormal Belief.” Cognition 123, no. 3 (2012): 335–346.
Spinoza, Baruch. Ethics. 1677. Geometric method as form.
Stagnaro, Michael N., et al. “Meta-Analyzing Intelligence and Religiosity Associations.” PLOS ONE 17, no. 1 (2022): e0262699.
Zuckerman, Miron, Jordan Silberman, and Judith A. Hall. “The Relation between Intelligence and Religiosity.” Personality and Social Psychology Review 17, no. 4 (2013): 325–354.
Zuckerman, Miron, et al. “The Negative Intelligence–Religiosity Relation: New and Confirming Evidence.” Personality and Social Psychology Bulletin 46, no. 6 (2020): 856–868.

neurology_sister.role: Systems-neurology sister paper. Same two lanes at neural grain.

paragraphs.text: Bottlenecks, Precision, and the Geometric Method
A systems-level sister paper: bottlenecks and precision as the load of a second map
Neuresthetics  ·  Version 7.1-N
How to read this paper

This is not a second copy of the genius study. It is the neurological grain of the same two lanes. Lane A cites functions and networks that reviews already treat as established. Lane B is a combination model: no hero circuit. Posterior cingulate and corpus callosum are named only as instances of a bottleneck principle. Predictive processing is the other half of the same principle. Default-mode language names the large-scale net some of those hubs sit in. Prefrontal override of child teleology is a supporting developmental idea, not a replacement architecture.

Window for compounding, if any: middle childhood into adolescence — when explicit theory-building can actually practice a geometric form. Early childhood still matters as the age of the agentive default. It is not the age of Ethics-style inference.
Table 1. Same functions, two standards of proof.
LANE A  —  WHAT IS ALREADY ON THE TABLE
Lane A. Systems facts, not a wiring diagram of God
A1. Dual process, not a soul

Religious cognition is not a dedicated organ. Dual-process work treats many supernatural beliefs as intuitive defaults that analytic processing can override. Individual differences in analytic style predict lower religious and paranormal belief after ordinary controls. Brief analytic primes can reduce reported belief. Later, larger samples still tie analytic thinking to belief change, not only to disbelief. Lane A stops there: style and belief covary; direction in experiments often runs style toward belief.
A2. Conflict has a known conflict signature

When two representations cannot both be acted on, dorsal anterior cingulate and anterior insula reliably show up. That is the ordinary neuroscience of conflict and of cognitive dissonance in scanner tasks — induced compliance, difficult choices, value-inconsistent reflection. Some of those designs also see posterior midline and prefrontal control. Lane A does not promote this into ‘the religious brain.’ It says only: holding incompatible commitments has a detectable conflict signature. A person who works all day in a lawful model and prays at night for an exemption is, at the level of function, a candidate for that signature. That is a hypothesis about a life, not a finding about a doctrine.
A3. Default-mode network as sense-making, PCC as a hub

The default-mode network is not idling. Reviews treat it as internally directed mentation and, in later formulations, as a sense-making system that integrates incoming events with long-timescale priors — self, story, situation. On the midline, posterior cingulate cortex is repeatedly described as a hub that talks to the rest of the network. That is why PCC appears in this paper at all. It is a documented integration node inside a documented sense-making net. It is not, in Lane A, the seat of theology.

Rumination and depression literatures find default-network hyperconnectivity in internally stuck thought. That is relevant only as a reminder that a sense-making net can loop. It does not license ‘incoherent religion equals depression.’
A4. Teleology is pruned, not erased

Young children explain nature with purpose far more broadly than adults do. That bias narrows with schooling and still returns in adults under time pressure. The interesting developmental fact for this project is the timing of the prune: elementary years into later childhood, not infancy. Formal scientific talk and mechanistic alternatives are what restrict the bias. That is why Lane B’s compounding window is middle childhood into adolescence rather than the toddler years. A two-year-old cannot run a geometric method. A ten-to-sixteen-year-old can begin to.
A5. Bottlenecks as ordinary anatomy

Some tissue is scarce integration tissue. Cortical hubs, including midline default hubs, sit on many paths. The corpus callosum is the large interhemispheric path. Calling both ‘bottlenecks’ is not a mystic claim. It is the statement that integration is capacity-limited. Anything that requires two incompatible situation-models to be kept live will use more of that capacity than one model. Lane A can say that as a resource argument. It cannot say that prayer, baptism, or Spinoza occupies a named voxel.
LANE B  —  COMBINATION MODEL
Lane B. One principle, several instances

Status. Labeled model. Combination, not a primary circuit. Predictive precision and bottleneck load are the same fact described twice: a high-precision exception prior is what forces a second model through a scarce integration channel.
B1. The exception prior

In predictive-processing language, perception and belief are inference under priors. Most priors are harmless. An interventionist personal God, used as a working prior rather than as poetry, is a special kind of prior: some observations are allowed to stand outside the lawful generative model. Weather, illness, victory, and in-group fortune can be attributed to an agent who is not bound by the rest of the model. That is high precision on exemptions.

A lawful-immanent schema does the opposite. Exceptions are low-precision. They are not-yet-known law, or noise, or the person’s ignorance. The generative model is not split. Pantheism and atheistic naturalism share that precision policy. They do not share the circle: pantheism keeps entity as both the mapped (Nature as God) and the mapping (Nature rendered in entity). The goal is reduced dissonance between mapping and mapped. Geometric method is how the shared stance is practiced: a definition binds, a proposition follows, a scholium does not reopen a miracle clause. The method is not Latin. It is the refusal to keep an exemption prior at high precision. Lane B’s extra claim is the circle, not the exemption-refusal alone.
B2. Why that lands on bottlenecks

A split model is expensive at integration sites. That is dissonance between mapping and mapped when a second map (a petitioner outside the rendering) is kept live next to the lawful one. Those copies have to be coordinated whenever the person thinks about cause, blame, hope, or death. Midline sense-making hubs are a natural place to feel that coordination. The callosum is another place if the two copies are also being run in styles that prefer different hemispheric coalitions — propositional structure in one, agentive narrative in the other. Lane B does not need that hemispheric story to be true. It only needs scarce integration. PCC and CC are two named instances of the same scarcity.

Default-mode language is the large-scale address of some of those hubs. If a person lives in a two-model cosmology, internally directed thought has more to reconcile. That can look like rumination, or like piety, or like nothing a questionnaire catches. The model does not equate religion with rumination. It says two high-precision models of cause are more work for a sense-making net than one.
B3. The developmental operator

Child cognition prefers agents and purposes. That default is not a religion yet. It is the raw material religions use. Schooling prunes it. Analytic control, slowly strengthening through later childhood and adolescence, is what makes the prune possible as an explicit act rather than as a habit picked up from adult talk.

Lane B’s compounding claim sits here. Content planted early as mere denial (‘there is no one in the thunder’) is cheap and unstable, and it flattens pantheism into atheism. The pantheist sentence is the circle: thunder is modeled as out-there and rendered in entity; a petitioner outside the rendering is a second map of the same mapped. Form practiced when formal reasoning comes online — middle childhood into adolescence — is the candidate for a dividend. The practice is geometric in the thin sense: say what a thing is, say what follows, do not reserve a clause. Prefrontal control is the supporting operator because that is the ordinary developmental story of overriding a salient intuition. It is not a third architecture. It is how an exemption prior gets its precision turned down.
B4. What the geometric method would be doing, functionally
Collapsing exemptions. Each completed inference that does not open a miracle clause is a training trial against a high-precision exception prior.
Keeping one situation model. Definitions act as shared latents. Later propositions write into the same model instead of into a second, petitionary model.
Spending bottleneck budget on structure rather than on reconciliation. The scarce channel still works. It works on one hierarchy.

Adult maintenance. The neuresthetic loop — map a stuck inference, modulate it by rerunning the form, watch a proxy — is the same operation after the window: close the gap between mapping and mapped. It can be done without the metaphysics. Lane B’s extra claim is that starting inside the circle, in the window, is cheaper than repairing two maps later.
B5. Faraday, again

A devout lawful physicist is predicted, not forbidden. If the active ingredient is the no-exemption form, Faraday already has it. If the active ingredient is the word pantheism, he is a problem. Lane B should prefer the first reading and then test whether metaphysics adds anything above form. That test is a living protocol, not a roster.
B6. Predictions at systems grain
Table B1. Proxies stay at tasks and reports until a circuit earns a name.
B7. What this paper will not say
That PCC ‘is’ the religious organ, or that callosal thickness is piety.
That DMN hyperconnectivity is Abrahamic religion.
That a historical genius list has already shown a plasticity effect.
That intelligence enhancement is a present application.
Joint close

Lane A: conflict has a signature, sense-making has a network, analytic style moves belief, child teleology prunes on a timetable that matches formal reasoning, integration is capacity-limited. Those are reusable facts.

Lane B: a high-precision exception prior is a second world-model forced through that limited capacity. That is the shared mechanism with naturalism. Pantheism’s extra is the circle — mapping of out-there happening in-there — so petition is a second map, and the work is dissonance between mapping and mapped. Geometric method is practiced refusal of the exception. Middle childhood into adolescence is when the refusal can be practiced as form. Posterior midline hubs and the callosum are two addresses of the same scarcity. Default-mode talk is the net those hubs sit in. Prefrontal control is the developmental tool that turns the default down.

If later work must pick a single slogan: not a region — a precision policy at a bottleneck, which is dissonance between mapping and mapped when a second map is forced through scarce tissue. That is the combination, said once.
References
Andrews-Hanna, Jessica R. “The Brain’s Default Network and Its Adaptive Role in Internal Mentation.” The Neuroscientist 18, no. 3 (2012): 251–270.
Gervais, Will M., and Ara Norenzayan. “Analytic Thinking Promotes Religious Disbelief.” Science 336, no. 6080 (2012): 493–496.
Harris, Sam, et al. “The Neural Correlates of Religious and Nonreligious Belief.” PLoS ONE 4, no. 10 (2009): e7272.
Izuma, Keise, et al. Neural and dissonance choice studies; see also van Veen et al., Nature Neuroscience 12 (2009): 1469–1474, dACC and anterior insula in induced compliance.
Kelemen, Deborah. “The Scope of Teleological Thinking in Preschool Children.” Cognition 70, no. 3 (1999): 241–272; and later pruning work into school age and adulthood under load.
Kapogiannis, Dimitrios, et al. “Cognitive and Neural Foundations of Religious Belief.” Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences 106, no. 12 (2009): 4876–4881.
Nguyen, Mai, and Uri Hasson. “The Default Mode Network: Where the Idiosyncratic Self Meets the Shared Social World.” Nature Reviews Neuroscience 22 (2021): 181–192.
Pennycook, Gordon, et al. “Analytic Cognitive Style Predicts Religious and Paranormal Belief.” Cognition 123, no. 3 (2012): 335–346.
van Veen, Vincent, et al. “Neural Activity Predicts Attitude Change in Cognitive Dissonance.” Nature Neuroscience 12 (2009): 1469–1474.
Zuckerman, Miron, Jordan Silberman, and Judith A. Hall. “The Relation between Intelligence and Religiosity.” Personality and Social Psychology Review 17, no. 4 (2013): 325–354.

paragraphs.text: Neuresthetics Genius Study
Data Book
Every table at the 2026-09-14 freeze, including the 77-system rubric and the 482-person roster.
1. How to read this file

This document is the data book in Word. It is not a results paper. Lane A papers (V7, V7.1) describe where remembered genius sits. Lane B is the labeled cultivation model: the circle of mapping and mapped — out-there modeled in-there — and reduced dissonance as the work. V7.1-N is the systems-neurology sister paper. Nothing here codes a person as LIO-high. The coding template is empty on purpose.

Frequency is inter-model consensus across five generators (Claude, DeepSeek, Gemini, ChatGPT, Grok), after alias merge. It is not genius intensity. Scores above 5 are stacked name-variants, not a sixth model.
2. Headline counts
3. Dictionary
4. LIO axes (person-level)
5. Coding rules
6. Belief systems — scores (n = 77)

Authorial five-axis rubric. Axes: logical self-consistency, resolution of known paradoxes, direct empirical compatibility, evidence vs revelation authority, predictive/explanatory success. Each 0–10. Total / 50. This is a map of official schemas, not a population parameter and not an IQ test.
Column key: L logical consistency · P paradox resolution · E empirical compatibility · V evidence vs revelation · X predictive/explanatory success.
7. Belief systems — scoring notes
Overall reasoning from the scoring corpus, one paragraph per system.

ATHE (50/50) — Atheism (naturalistic/materialistic – no gods + philosophical naturalism). Atheism achieves a perfect score as the most parsimonious system, fully embracing naturalism and science without unnecessary metaphysical additions, making it highly coherent and empirically robust.
AGNOS (49/50) — Agnosticism. Agnosticism promotes intellectual humility, scoring near-perfect for its evidence-based skepticism and avoidance of unsubstantiated commitments.

BRGHTS (49/50) — Brights (The Brights Movement). The Brights Movement scores highly for its evidence-based naturalism and civic focus, serving as a practical extension of atheism with strong coherence.
EMPIR (49/50) — Empiricism. Empiricism is foundational to science, scoring high for its evidence-driven approach, with minor deduction for induction limitations.
ETHCUL (49/50) — Ethical Culture (Ethical Humanism). Ethical Culture scores highly for its rational, action-oriented ethics, serving as a secular moral framework with excellent coherence.
PANT (49/50) — Pantheism as the circle: entity applied to Nature and Nature rendered in entity. Not God deleted. Petition splits mapping from mapped. Scores near-perfect for a no-exemption cosmos.

RATN (49/50) — Rationalism. Rationalism excels in logical rigor and evidence prioritization, scoring high overall but docked slightly for occasional over-reliance on deduction in non-empirical contexts.

SECHUM (49/50) — Secular Humanism. Secular Humanism scores near-perfect by integrating rational ethics with empirical science, promoting human flourishing without dogma, though its focus on welfare adds a minor subjective layer.
SUNASM (49/50) — Sunday Assembly. Sunday Assembly achieves near-perfect scores by providing a rational, community-driven framework that mirrors religious benefits without dogma.
PRAG (48/50) — Pragmatism. Pragmatism excels in practical, evidence-based problem-solving, with a high score reflecting its adaptability and real-world focus.
ARIST (47/50) — Aristotelianism. Aristotelianism lays foundational empirical and logical groundwork, scoring high despite historical limitations.
EFFALT (47/50) — Effective Altruism. Effective Altruism is highly coherent, focusing on rational benevolence with strong empirical backing.
TRNSHM (47/50) — Transhumanism. Transhumanism scores high for its rational, tech-driven optimism, bridging current science with future potential.

ABSURD (46/50) — Absurdism. Absurdism scores high for its honest confrontation with life's irrationality, promoting authentic living with strong empirical ties to human psychology, though inherently non-predictive in physical domains.

CYNIC (46/50) — Cynicism. Cynicism scores high for its empirical naturalism and practical virtue ethics, promoting self-sufficiency and critiquing conventions, making it a robust philosophy for personal coherence despite its ancient origins.
EPICUR (46/50) — Epicureanism. Epicureanism balances pleasure with reason, scoring high for its empirical roots in atomism and ethics.
EXIST (46/50) — Existentialism. Existentialism empowers individual meaning-making with strong psychological insight.
NIHIL (46/50) — Nihilism. Nihilism provides a stark, evidence-based critique of meaning, with high coherence in its rejection.

OBJCT (46/50) — Objectivism (Ayn Rand's philosophy). Objectivism scores high for its rational, integrated approach to reality and ethics, promoting individualism with strong empirical ties, but slightly limited by its prescriptive economic views.

SCEPT (46/50) — Scepticism (Skepticism). Scepticism scores high for its rigorous promotion of doubt and evidence, fostering critical thinking essential for genius-level inquiry, though it may limit absolute commitments.
STOIC (46/50) — Stoicism. Stoicism provides practical wisdom with strong rational and empirical ties, ideal for personal coherence.

KANT (45/50) — Kantianism. Kantianism scores high for its logical rigor and emphasis on universal duty, providing a foundational deontological framework, though slightly limited by abstraction from real-world variability.

PHENOM (45/50) — Phenomenology. Phenomenology scores high for its methodical exploration of experience, providing foundational insights into consciousness with strong logical and empirical ties, though focused more on description than prediction.

UTIL (45/50) — Utilitarianism. Utilitarianism scores high for its empirical and rational approach to ethics, optimizing for collective good with practical applications, though slightly limited by measurement abstractions and potential oversimplification.

PANDEI (44/50) — Pandeism. Pandeism scores high for its elegant synthesis of theism and naturalism, providing a coherent, empirically friendly alternative to interventionist religions, though slightly limited by its speculative transformative premise.

PANEND (44/50) — Panendeism. Panendeism scores high for its elegant fusion of deism and pantheism, providing a conscious yet non-interventionist divine model with strong logical and empirical alignment.

CLASS_THEISM (43/50) — Classical Theism (Aristotelian-Thomistic-Islamic Peripatetic). One of the highest-coherence theistic systems; used by Aristotle, Al-Farabi, Avicenna, Averroes, Maimonides, Aquinas, Leibniz, and many others.

DETERM (43/50) — Determinism. Determinism scores high for its logical rigor and alignment with empirical causality, providing a foundational view of reality, but tempered by ongoing debates in quantum physics and free will.

LVSAT (43/50) — LaVeyan Satanism (Church of Satan). LaVeyan Satanism scores relatively high as an atheistic philosophy promoting rational individualism, with strong empirical and logical alignment, though its symbolic elements slightly limit predictive scope.

PANENT (42/50) — Panentheism (Process Theology, some Kabbalah/Advaita forms). Panentheism scores high for its dynamic integration of divinity with the universe, providing philosophical depth and compatibility with science, though slightly limited by transcendent metaphysical elements.

DEISM (41/50) — Deism. Deism achieves a high score for its rational reconciliation of a creator with empirical science, avoiding the pitfalls of interventionist theism, though docked slightly for the unprovable deistic assumption.

HEDON (41/50) — Hedonism. Hedonism scores relatively high for its empirical ties to human psychology and consistent pleasure-based ethics, offering practical guidance for well-being, but limited by potential oversimplification of complex motivations.

PANPSY (39/50) — Panpsychism (consciousness inherent in matter). Panpsychism scores moderately high as an innovative philosophy bridging consciousness and matter, with strong logical appeal but tempered by speculative elements and incomplete empirical support.

IDEAL (38/50) — Idealism. Idealism scores moderately due to its innovative mind-centered view of reality, providing philosophical depth but constrained by challenges in empirical verification and material compatibility.

BUDDH (37/50) — Buddhism. Buddhism scores relatively high due to its profound philosophical and practical approach to ending suffering, blending ethics and meditation with strong psychological alignment, but tempered by metaphysical elements like rebirth that reduce empirical compatibility.

PLATO (37/50) — Platonism. Platonism scores moderately high due to its influential theory of ideal forms, providing philosophical depth for reality and ethics, but limited by abstract nature and modest empirical alignment.

JAIN (36/50) — Jainism. Jainism scores relatively high due to its rigorous ethical system and focus on non-violence, providing strong moral coherence, but limited by metaphysical elements like karma and souls that reduce empirical alignment.

SOLIP (35/50) — Solipsism. Solipsism scores moderately high for its radical logical purity and focus on personal certainty, but is limited by its dismissal of empirical intersubjectivity and practical applicability.

BAHAI (34/50) — Bahá’í Faith. Bahá’í Faith scores moderately high due to its innovative emphasis on global unity and progressive revelation, fostering ethical and social coherence, but constrained by revelatory authority over full empirical alignment.

ANIM (32/50) — Animism. Animism scores moderately as a spiritual philosophy emphasizing universal life and harmony, providing cultural depth but constrained by supernatural assumptions and modest empirical alignment.

CAODAI (32/50) — Caodaism. Caodaism scores moderately due to its innovative syncretism promoting religious unity, offering ethical and spiritual coherence but limited by revelatory elements and modest empirical alignment.

CHNFOLK (32/50) — Chinese Folk Religion (Shenism). Chinese Folk Religion scores moderately due to its flexible syncretism for daily life and harmony, blending traditions effectively but constrained by supernatural elements and cultural authority over empirical rigor.
HYLO (32/50) — Hylozoism. Hylozoism scores moderately as a philosophical view animating all matter, providing conceptual unity but constrained by speculative nature and modest empirical alignment.

CONFUC (32/50) — Philosophical Confucianism. Confucianism scores moderately due to its profound ethical system for societal harmony, grounded in human relationships, but limited by traditional authority and modest empirical scope beyond social sciences.

SHINTO (32/50) — Shinto. Shinto scores moderately due to its elegant focus on natural harmony and ritual purity, offering cultural and ethical coherence but constrained by supernatural elements and traditional authority over empirical rigor.

TAO (32/50) — Taoism (Daoism). Taoism scores moderately due to its profound emphasis on natural harmony and practical wisdom, blending philosophy and religion effectively, but constrained by mystical elements and traditional authority over rigorous empirical methods.

HINDU (28/50) — Hinduism (Sanatana Dharma). Hinduism scores moderately due to its profound philosophical depth and ethical systems, accommodating diverse paths to enlightenment, but limited by supernatural claims and scriptural authority over empirical evidence.

HEATH (27/50) — Heathenry (Ásatrú/Norse-Germanic Paganism). Heathenry scores moderately due to its cultural revival of Germanic polytheism, emphasizing honor and nature, but limited by supernatural elements and reconstructionist authority over empirical rigor.

HELLEN (27/50) — Hellenismos (Greek Reconstructionist Paganism). Hellenismos scores moderately due to its thoughtful reconstruction of Greek polytheism, blending philosophy and ethics, but limited by mythic elements and lack of empirical support.

KEMET (27/50) — Kemetism (Kemetic Orthodoxy/Egyptian Reconstructionism). Kemetism scores moderately due to its revival of ancient Egyptian balance and justice principles, offering ethical coherence but limited by mythic reconstruction and lack of empirical rigor.

RODNOV (27/50) — Rodnovery (Slavic Native Faith). Rodnovery scores moderately due to its cultural revival of Slavic traditions, emphasizing nature and ancestry, but limited by mythic elements and lack of empirical rigor.

WICCA (27/50) — Wicca. Wicca scores moderately due to its nature-centered and magical framework, offering ethical and communal coherence but limited by supernatural elements and subjective authority over empirical rigor.

ABORIG (26/50) — Aboriginal Traditions (Australian Aboriginal Dreamtime). Aboriginal Traditions score moderately due to their deep connection to land and ancestors through Dreamtime narratives, offering rich cultural coherence but limited by oral revelation and lack of empirical grounding.

BON (26/50) — Bön (Tibetan indigenous religion). Bön scores moderately due to its ancient shamanistic roots and focus on natural harmony, offering cultural and spiritual coherence but limited by revelatory elements and lack of empirical rigor.

NATAM (26/50) — Native American Traditions. Native American Traditions score moderately due to their profound connection to nature and ancestors, offering rich cultural and ethical coherence but limited by reliance on oral revelation and lack of empirical rigor.

SANTER (26/50) — Santería (Lucumí/Regla de Ocha). Santería scores moderately due to its rich syncretic traditions and emphasis on spiritual balance, offering cultural coherence but limited by supernatural elements and lack of empirical rigor.

VODUN (26/50) — Vodun (Voodoo/West African Vodun). Vodun scores moderately due to its emphasis on spiritual balance and communal practices, offering rich cultural coherence but limited by supernatural elements and lack of empirical rigor.

ANTHRO (25/50) — Anthroposophy. Anthroposophy scores moderately due to its ambitious integration of spirit and science, offering innovative applications but limited by revelatory and unempirical elements.

CHAOSM (25/50) — Chaos Magick. Chaos Magick scores moderately due to its innovative, flexible approach to personal empowerment and magick, balanced by subjective elements that reduce empirical and predictive strength.

4THWAY (25/50) — Fourth Way (Gurdjieff's teachings). Fourth Way scores moderately due to its integrative spiritual approach and focus on self-awakening, balanced by esoteric elements that reduce empirical alignment.
HERMET (25/50) — Hermeticism. Hermeticism scores moderately due to its esoteric and symbolic approach to enlightenment, balanced by limited empirical grounding and reliance on ancient revelations.

SIKH (25/50) — Sikhism. Sikhism scores moderately due to its strong ethical coherence and emphasis on equality and service, which foster social harmony, but its revelatory foundation and supernatural aspects limit empirical and predictive alignment.

THEOS (25/50) — Theosophy. Theosophy scores moderately due to its ambitious syncretic approach to spiritual unity, balanced by unverified esoteric claims and reliance on revelation over empirical methods.

DRUZE (23/50) — Druze Faith. Druze Faith scores moderately low due to its esoteric and revelatory focus, though it provides a cohesive framework for monotheism and reincarnation within a secretive tradition.

MANDAE (23/50) — Mandaeism. Mandaeism scores moderately low due to its esoteric gnostic focus and reliance on revelation over empirical methods, though it provides a unique framework for spiritual ascent and ethical living.

YAZID (23/50) — Yazidism (Yezidism). Yazidism scores moderately low due to its esoteric and oral-based nature, emphasizing spiritual liberation through reincarnation and angelic veneration within a monotheistic frame.

ZORO (23/50) — Zoroastrianism (Mazdayasna). Zoroastrianism scores moderately low due to its revelatory dualism and limited empirical alignment, though it pioneered ethical monotheism influencing later religions.

CHRIST (22/50) — Christianity. Christianity provides a comprehensive faith-based framework for salvation and ethics, but its reliance on supernatural revelation over empirical evidence limits its scientific alignment.

ISLAM (22/50) — Islam. Islam provides a comprehensive monotheistic framework emphasizing submission and ethics, but its reliance on revelation over empirical evidence limits its alignment with scientific metrics.
JUDA (22/50) — Judaism. Judaism provides a rich ethical and covenantal framework with historical depth, but its reliance on revelation over empirical evidence limits its score on scientific metrics.

MORMON (21/50) — Mormonism (The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints). Mormonism scores moderately low due to its heavy reliance on unique revelations and scriptures over empirical evidence, though it provides strong community and family-oriented coherence.

CLTHEI (20/50) — Classical Theism (personal, interventionist Creator God). Classical Theism scores low due to persistent logical paradoxes like the problem of evil and reliance on revelation over empirical evidence, though it provides a foundational framework for many Abrahamic religions.

THSAT (20/50) — Theistic Satanism (Joy of Satan or similar). Theistic Satanism scores low due to its supernatural focus and reliance on revelation, though it provides a rebellious framework for some adherents.

THELEM (20/50) — Thelema (Crowley/Ordo Templi Orientis). Thelema scores low overall due to its heavy reliance on occult revelation and unverified magick, though it fosters individual empowerment and creative spiritual exploration.

FALUNG (17/50) — Falun Gong (Falun Dafa). Falun Gong scores low due to its reliance on supernatural claims and authority over evidence, making it less compatible with empirical science despite ethical appeals.

RAEL (17/50) — Raëlism (Raëlian Movement). Raëlism scores low due to its reliance on unverified extraterrestrial claims and revelation over evidence, positioning it as a modern UFO-based movement with limited empirical grounding.
SCIENT (17/50) — Scientology. Scientology scores low due to its pseudoscientific claims and reliance on founder authority over empirical evidence, despite structured self-improvement appeals.
